newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul analysts welcome raised share holding limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul analysts welcome raised share holding limit.

text.p: Stock market analysts welcomed on Tuesday the plan to raise the foreign share ownership limit on October 1 and said stock prices were expected to gain by around 10 percent from the current level by late this year.
They predicted banking and insurance shares will attract the most buying interest while blue-chip manufacturing firms are likely to remain weak due to economic woes.

"I think it will be a boost for the market in October, a quick bounce similar to what we saw in April," said Lee Keun-mo, head of research at ING Baring Securities, referring to the April 1 increase of the limit to 18 percent from 15 percent.

The Finance and Economy Ministry announced on Tuesday it would raise the foreign share ownership limit further to 20 percent on October 1. The move was in line with the ministry's earlier plan to raise the ceiling within this year.
Analysts said the composite stock price index was expected to test the psychologically important 900-point level within this year, compared with Tuesday's closing of 769.80.
"The measure will greatly help ease the imbalance between demand and supply on the market," said Kim Kyeong-shin, head of research at Daeyu Securities.
Analysts saw the ceiling increase translating into an additional influx of about 1.5 trillion won in foreign funds into the local stock market.
"Investors will continue to shun the manufacturing stocks at least until they see signs that the economy reached the bottom," said a fund manager at Korea Investment Trust Co.
The announcement had no immediate impact on the stock market on Tuesday because it came after the end of trading.
